title: conflicts and stashing
goal: B4 Resolve a conflict deliberately, and park work you are not ready to commit
startWith: Create a conflict on purpose: two branches editing the same line.

newIdeas.plain: Both sides changed the same region. Git stops and hands you both versions.
In a merge, ours is the branch you are on. In a rebase they swap — that reversal is the whole trap.
A stack of uncommitted changes, stored off to the side.

tasks.do: Manufacture a conflict, read the markers, resolve it by hand

blocks.label: terminal
blocks.body:
git switch -c a && echo 'from a' > conflict.txt && git add -A && git commit -m a
git switch main && git switch -c b && echo 'from b' > conflict.txt && git add -A && git commit -m b
git switch main && git merge a && git merge b    # the second one conflicts
git status
git diff --diff-filter=U

blocks.label: IntelliJ
blocks.body: The conflict dialog's Merge… button opens the three-pane merge tool: theirs, result, yours. Materially better than editing markers by hand — press Apply non-conflicting changes first.

tasks.do: Finish the merge, or abandon it

blocks.label: terminal
blocks.body:
git add conflict.txt && git commit    # finish
git merge --abort                     # or: back to before the merge

tasks.do: Take one whole side without editing
tasks.why: For generated files (lock files, snapshots) the answer is “all of theirs”, and hand-merging them is wasted time.

blocks.label: terminal
blocks.body:
git checkout --ours package-lock.json
git checkout --theirs package-lock.json
git add package-lock.json

tasks.do: Stash work in progress, switch branch, bring it back

blocks.label: terminal
blocks.body:
git stash push -m "half-done parser"
git stash list
git switch main
git stash pop              # apply and drop
git stash apply stash@{0}  # apply and keep

blocks.label: IntelliJ
blocks.body: Git → Shelve Changes is the IDE's own version, with a diff in the Shelf tab. Git → Uncommitted Changes → Stash uses real git stash when you need it visible from the terminal.

check.expect: the command runs (an empty list is fine)

tasks.do: Turn on rerere so you resolve the same conflict once
tasks.why: Long-lived branches hit identical conflicts on every rebase. rerere replays your recorded resolution.

proof.expect: a merge you resolved by hand
proof.note: A conflict is a task, not an emergency.

doneWhen: You reach for the IDE merge tool automatically, and never commit a file containing <<<<<<<.

lessons.title: Shelve — the IDE's stash
lessons.teach: Git → Shelve Changes parks your work with a name and a diff you can browse in the Shelf tab. Use real git stash (Git → Uncommitted Changes → Stash) only when the terminal needs to see it too.

lessons.title: The three-pane merge tool
lessons.teach: On a conflict, press Merge… rather than editing markers. Left is theirs, right is yours, the middle is the result you are building — and Apply non-conflicting changes clears the noise so only the real disagreement is left.
lessons.fallbackTip: git mergetool, or edit the <<<<<<< markers by hand.
